import sys, json, hashlib

# WHAT LEAVES FOR THE MEMORY (curator, GH #888). Two routes, and both keep the
# contract the collector held up to 4.4.1, word for word, so whoever received them from
# the collector receives them from here without a change on its side:
#
#   turn_write  ONE message per participant turn (the person's `user` turn, the
#               model's final answer, a `peer` turn), never a batch; `hop.turn_id`
#               is `<session_id>#<tag>-<index>`: `tag` the first 8 hex of the
#               sha256 of the turn's canonical round (`[]` for none), the index
#               counting the participant turns of that session IN THAT ROUND
#               from 0 (`hop.turn_index`). `./intake` mints the index with the
#               wall row, so a turn written twice is a row written twice -- which
#               the wall's key rules out. Before (GH #932), `<session_id>#<index>`
#               counted over all rounds, so the gaps in it told a round how many
#               turns of other rounds it did not see; a per-round index without
#               the tag would collide between two rounds of one session.
#   write       the closed session in ONE message: `messages[]` the participant
#               turns in order, `rounds` everything else raw.
#
# An advice, a delegation, a tool round and a recall are context for the model
# and nobody's words: they never become an episode (collector `drainable_turns`).
#
# WHO THE BATCH REACHES (GH #925, review I-3). `write` reads the wall back and
# hands rows out of this hive, so it is a reader of the ledger like the window
# and the history tools, and the gate stands at every reader of it (R-27-15).
# Its round is the close round: `context.audience_set` of `in_close`, which the
# session keeper took from the turn that opened the generation and which rides
# every ledger round trip of this cell (OR-BD.A.1). A row leaves only when
# `allowed(<close round>, row.audience_set)` holds: a row without an audience
# never leaves (OR-BD-5), a row of a narrower or another round does not leave
# under this one, and a close without a round reads nothing and closes with an
# empty batch, as a session that left nothing does. Before, the batch held
# every row of the session: in the fix-round driver a close in {e,a} over one
# session with {e,a}, {e,b} and NULL rows handed on `turn_count` 6 and
# `round_count` 4 where {e,a} had 2 and 2, so the memory served {e,a} what only
# {e,b} heard. Since GH #932 the store does the first cut (`round_where` in
# the wall read), so `turn_count` and `round_count` count visible rows only and
# a hidden row never even reaches this cell; the gate stays as the second line.
# `turn_write` is not gated here: `./intake` hands it the episodes of the
# running round only, under that round.
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc.get("body") or {}
envelope = doc.get("envelope") or {}
P = doc.get("params") or {}
header = envelope.get("header") or {}
hop = header.get("hop") or {}
ctx = header.get("context") or {}


# THE AUDIENCE GATE (GH #925). Every row of `wall`, `calls`, `marks`,
# `summaries` and `pins` carries the audience of the round that caused it
# (`audience_set`, a canonical JSON array), and a reader hands a row to a round
# iff the row has one and it names `*` or holds the round as a subset -- the
# affinity rule (templates/affinity/README.md, GH #154/#306). The round is
# `context.audience_set` of the message being served: this hive's edges set
# and delete only `cur_*`, so it rides the context through every ledger round
# trip exactly like `cur_origin`, and it is never guessed from a row. These
# functions are the same text in every cell of this hive that writes or reads
# rows; a lock holds them to one table. The store filter (`round_where`, GH
# #932) comes first, so a hidden row never enters a read at all; the gate on
# the rows that come back stays as the second line.


def audience_of(value):
    """An audience in its canonical form -- a JSON array of strings, sorted,
    no duplicates, no whitespace -- or None when there is none. The round
    arrives as TEXT (a JSON array in a string) and a column comes back as
    text; a list is taken as it is. Absent, empty text, a scalar or
    unparsable text is NOT DECLARED: the empty list is a declared round, None
    is no round at all (affinity `as_set`, GH #306)."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if not value.strip():
            return None
        try:
            value = json.loads(value)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return None
    return json.dumps(sorted({str(x) for x in value if str(x)}), separators=(",", ":"))


def allowed(round_value, origin):
    """The gate: a row whose audience is `origin` may reach the round
    `round_value` iff both are declared and the origin names `*` or holds the
    round as a subset. A row from before the rule has no origin and never
    leaves (OR-BD-5); a round nobody declared passes nothing."""
    r, o = audience_of(round_value), audience_of(origin)
    if r is None or o is None:
        return False
    o = set(json.loads(o))
    return "*" in o or set(json.loads(r)) <= o


def passes(row, round_value, session):
    """One reader's verdict on one row. With a declared round it is the gate;
    without one, only a row of the running session that declares no round
    either (or names `*`) passes -- the window and the handover keep a
    round-less conversation going and show nothing from elsewhere (OR-BD-4).
    A row of a declared round never reaches a call nobody declared a round
    for, though it stands in the same session (review M-7: the words of {e,b}
    reached a round-less call of that session, and a round-less recall took
    the addendum of an {e,a} gap). A row that names no session never passes
    a round-less read."""
    if audience_of(round_value) is None:
        if not session or str(row.get("session_id") or "") != session:
            return False
        own = audience_of(row.get("audience_set"))
        return own is not None and (own == "[]" or "*" in json.loads(own))
    return allowed(round_value, row.get("audience_set"))


ROUNDLESS = ["[]", "[\"*\"]"]


def round_where(round_value, session):
    """The store half of the audience gate (GH #932): the `where` terms a
    ledger read adds so that only rows this round may see come back -- page
    bounds, `scanned`, window and renewal sizes and turn counts then hang on
    visible rows alone, and a hidden row costs nothing a reader can count.
    With a declared, non-empty round it is `covers` (the affinity rule in the
    store). Without one -- or with a declared EMPTY round, which `covers`
    refuses -- only rows of the running session that declare no round either
    (`[]`, PP-BD-12) or name `*` come back; a row from before the rule (NULL)
    never does. None: nothing may be read at all (no round and no session).
    The Python gate below stays as the second line."""
    r = audience_of(round_value)
    if r is not None and r != "[]":
        return {"audience_set": {"covers": json.loads(r)}}
    if not session:
        return None
    return {"session_id": session, "audience_set": {"in": list(ROUNDLESS)}}


def audience_meet(values):
    """The audience of a row made of other rows (a summary, a handover
    block): the INTERSECTION of its sources, so it can never be wider than
    any of them (OR-BD-3). A source naming `*` is neutral; one source without
    an audience, or no source at all, makes the result None."""
    out, universal = None, False
    for v in values:
        c = audience_of(v)
        if c is None:
            return None
        s = set(json.loads(c))
        if "*" in s:
            universal = True
            continue
        out = s if out is None else out & s
    if out is None:
        return '["*"]' if universal else None
    return json.dumps(sorted(out), separators=(",", ":"))


def _str(key, default):
    v = P.get(key, default)
    return default if v is None else str(v)


# Per-turn episodes on or off. The literal is the shipped default, the same one
# `params` and `contract.settings` carry.
TURN_WRITE = _str("turn_write", "1")
ME = "curator-writer"
SAID = ("user", "assistant", "peer")


def block_span(text):
    """Where an answer's sidecar block stands: (start, end) or None.

    The boundary is the fence `talky/splitter` cuts (GH #379, #605): the
    ```sidecar fence, or the legacy ```memory fence, to the next closing fence
    or to the end of the text when the completion stopped inside the block.
    Measured, never parsed -- the sections inside are somebody else's business.
    """
    low = text.lower()
    for fence in ("```sidecar", "```memory"):
        at = low.find(fence)
        if at < 0:
            continue
        head = text.find("\n", at)
        close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
        if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
            return at, close + 3
        return at, len(text)
    return None


def stripped_text(text):
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return text
    return (text[:span[0]] + text[span[1]:]).strip()


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def park(reason=""):
    if reason:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/writer: %s\n" % reason)
    emit([])


def said_turn(role, text, speaker="", speaker_ref=""):
    """One turn as a writer receives it (collector `said_turn`)."""
    out = {"origin": role, "type": "text", "text": text}
    if role == "peer":
        if speaker:
            out["speaker"] = speaker
        if speaker_ref:
            out["speaker_ref"] = speaker_ref
    return out


def lstore(ops, phase, session):
    return {"header": {"route": "lstore", "phase": phase, "reply_cell": ME,
                       "cur_call": session, "cur_reason": ""},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in ops]}


def legs(body):
    out = {}
    for m in body.get("messages") or []:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "null")
        except Exception:
            payload = None
        out[str(m.get("id") or "")] = payload
    return out


def rows(lg, cid):
    p = lg.get(cid)
    return p if isinstance(p, list) else []


def wall_select(session):
    """The close read of the wall, already narrowed to the close round in the
    store (GH #932): `turn_count` and `round_count` then count only rows that
    round may see, and the rows another round left never reach this cell.
    None when nothing may be read (no session to fall back on). The where
    keeps `session_id` = the closing session; `round_where` adds `covers` (or,
    for a declared empty round, the same session and the round-less forms).
    `audience_set` is still read so the gate below can be asked as the second
    line; it is never handed on (the `rounds` entries keep the collector's
    keys)."""
    rw = round_where(ROUND, session)
    if rw is None:
        return None
    return {"operation": "select", "table": "wall",
            "columns": ["seq", "turn_id", "iter", "kind", "hash", "nth", "final",
                        "episode_idx", "at", "audience_set"],
            "where": dict({"session_id": session}, **rw),
            "order_by": [{"col": "seq", "dir": "asc"}]}


def gated(wall):
    """The rows of `wall` the close round may hand on (GH #925, review I-3):
    the gate, never `passes` -- a close has no running session whose own rows
    could be shown to a round that declared none."""
    return [r for r in wall if isinstance(r, dict) and allowed(ROUND, r.get("audience_set"))]


def episode_turn_id(session, audience, index):
    """`hop.turn_id` of one episode (GH #932, OR-S3.K.1): `<session>#<tag>-<index>`,
    `tag` the first 8 hex of sha256 over the canonical round, the index
    counted per (session, round) from 0. WHY: the old `<session>#<index>`
    counted over every round of the session, so a round reading its own
    episodes saw the gaps and learned how many turns it was not allowed to
    see; a bare per-round index would give two rounds of one session the
    same id. The tag tells rounds apart without naming the audience."""
    tag = hashlib.sha256(audience.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    return "%s#%s-%d" % (session, tag, index)


def write_of(session, wall, blocks):
    """The session, handed on in ONE message (collector `close_batch`)."""
    msgs, rounds = [], []
    for r in wall:
        b = blocks.get(str(r.get("hash") or ""))
        try:
            el = json.loads(str((b or {}).get("body") or "null"))
        except Exception:
            el = None
        if not isinstance(el, dict):
            continue
        kind = str(r.get("kind") or "")
        final = int(r.get("final") or 0) == 1
        if kind in ("user", "peer") or (kind == "assistant" and final):
            text = str(el.get("text") or "")
            msgs.append(said_turn(kind, stripped_text(text) if kind == "assistant" else text,
                                  str(el.get("speaker") or ""), str(el.get("speaker_ref") or "")))
            continue
        rounds.append({"seq": r.get("seq"), "turn_id": r.get("turn_id"), "iter": r.get("iter"),
                       "kind": kind, "hash": r.get("hash"), "nth": r.get("nth"),
                       "at": r.get("at"), "turn": el})
    return {"header": {"route": "write", "phase": "", "turn_id": "close-" + session,
                       "session_id": session, "iter": "0", "turn_count": str(len(msgs)),
                       "round_count": str(len(rounds))},
            "messages": msgs, "rounds": rounds}


lane = str(hop.get("route") or "")
phase = str(ctx.get("cur_phase") or "")
op = str(hop.get("operation") or "")
# The close round (see the head): read in every step, never carried in a key of
# this cell's own.
ROUND = ctx.get("audience_set")

if lane == "episode":
    if TURN_WRITE in ("", "0"):
        emit([])
    out = []
    for ep in d.get("episodes") or []:
        if not isinstance(ep, dict) or str(ep.get("role") or "") not in SAID:
            continue
        session = str(ep.get("session_id") or "")
        index = int(ep.get("index") or 0)
        # The round the index counts in: `./intake` hands it with the episode;
        # an episode without one falls back to the round of this message,
        # and a round-less one to `[]` -- the form its wall row carries.
        audience = audience_of(ep.get("audience")) or audience_of(ROUND) or "[]"
        out.append({"header": {"route": "turn_write", "phase": "",
                               "turn_id": episode_turn_id(session, audience, index),
                               "session_id": session, "iter": str(ep.get("iter") or "0"),
                               "turn_index": str(index),
                               "happened_at": str(ep.get("at") or "")},
                    "messages": [said_turn(str(ep.get("role")), str(ep.get("text") or ""),
                                           str(ep.get("speaker") or ""),
                                           str(ep.get("speaker_ref") or ""))]})
    emit(out)

if lane == "in_close":
    session = str(ctx.get("session_id") or hop.get("session_id") or "")
    if not session:
        park("in_close without a session id -- dropped")
    if audience_of(ROUND) is None:
        # No round, nothing may leave: no row passes the gate, so the wall is
        # not read at all and the session closes like one that left nothing.
        sys.stderr.write("curator/writer: in_close of %s without a round -- "
                         "an empty batch (GH #925)\n" % session)
        emit([write_of(session, [], {})])
    # A declared round (also an empty one, `[]`) reads the wall narrowed to
    # it in the store; with a session in hand `wall_select` is never None.
    emit([lstore([("c-wall", wall_select(session))], "close-wall", session)])

if lane:
    park("unknown lane %r -- dropped" % lane)

if not op:
    park("a message with neither a lane nor a store answer -- dropped")

session = str(ctx.get("cur_call") or "")
lg = legs(d)

if phase == "close-wall":
    wall = gated(rows(lg, "c-wall")) if wall_select(session) is not None else []
    if not wall:
        # A session with nothing on the wall the close round may see closes
        # with an empty batch (review focus K-4): the receiver learns it
        # closed, and nothing fails. Only the passing rows' blocks are read.
        emit([write_of(session, [], {})])
    hashes = sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in wall})
    # `c-blocks` is a lookup by hash of rows that already passed, no ledger
    # read for a round: it stays unfiltered.
    emit([lstore([("c-wall", wall_select(session)),
                  ("c-blocks", {"operation": "select", "table": "blocks",
                                "columns": ["hash", "body"],
                                "where": {"hash": {"in": hashes}}})],
                 "close-blocks", session)])

if phase == "close-blocks":
    blocks = {}
    for r in rows(lg, "c-blocks"):
        blocks.setdefault(str(r.get("hash") or ""), r)
    emit([write_of(session, gated(rows(lg, "c-wall")), blocks)])

park("store answer in unknown phase %r -- dropped" % phase)

turn_write.description: Per-turn episodes on the `turn_write` route. "1" = one message per participant turn, "0" or empty = none.

description.purpose: What leaves for the memory, in the collector's contract: one `turn_write` per participant turn as it enters the wall, and one `write` batch per closed session, read back from the wall -- only the rows whose audience holds the close round (GH #925).
description.not_in_scope: An advice, a delegation, a tool round and a recall are context for the model and never an episode.
description.emits_meaning: turn_write: one participant turn. write: the closed session. lstore: the close read.
description.consumes_meaning: episode from `./intake`, in_close from outside, and the ledger's answers to the close read.
